m01-variables-robot-memory.title: Try it: set the variable
m01-variables-robot-memory.brief: The robot starts on A1 facing north. Reach the flag on E5 using no more than 3 blocks. Shelves block C1, C3, D3 and E2.

m02-loops-do-it-again.title: Try it: climb the stairs
m02-loops-do-it-again.brief: The robot starts on A1 facing north. Climb the staircase to the flag on D4. Build the loop body with no more than 4 blocks, then set the repeat count.

m03-algorithms-step-by-step.title: Try it: order the delivery algorithm
m03-algorithms-step-by-step.brief: A line-following robot must deliver a package to a shelf and come back. Move the steps into the order the robot should run them, then check.

items.text: Calibrate the light sensor on black and white
items.why: The robot cannot follow the line until its sensor knows what black and white look like.
With a calibrated sensor, the robot can now follow the line toward the shelf.
The robot has to be at the shelf before it lets go of anything.
Now the package lands on the shelf instead of the start line.

items.text: Turn around and drive back to the start
items.why: The delivery is done, so the robot can return.

m04-sensors-how-robots-notice.title: Try it: match the sensor to the job
m04-sensors-how-robots-notice.brief: Pick the best sensor for each robot job. Name what you need to know first, then choose the sensor that measures it.

jobs.why: Ultrasonic measures distance in centimetres by timing an echo.

jobs.job: Follow a black line on a white mat
jobs.why: The light sensor reads about 8 over black tape and about 85 over the white mat.

jobs.job: Know the bumper has reached the shelf
jobs.why: The touch sensor reports pressed or released.
The gyro measures how far the robot has turned, in degrees.

m05-challenge-warehouse-run.title: Try it: the warehouse run
m05-challenge-warehouse-run.brief: Cross the warehouse from A1 (facing north) to the loading dock on F6. Shelves block B1 to B4 and D3 to D6. Stay within 14 blocks.

m06-the-design-loop.title: Try it: order the design loop
m06-the-design-loop.brief: Emma's team is building a ping-pong ball gripper. Put the five stages of their project in order, then check.

items.text: Ask: the ball is 40 mm wide, weighs 2.7 g, and must be lifted 10 cm
items.why: Ask comes first: state the problem and its limits before any ideas.

items.text: Imagine: sketch three different gripper ideas
items.why: Brainstorm many ideas before choosing one.

items.text: Plan: pick the claw idea, draw it and list the parts
items.why: Plan turns one chosen idea into a drawing and a parts list.

items.text: Create: build a cardboard and servo prototype
items.why: Create builds the plan. It does not need to be pretty.

items.text: Test and improve: 7 of 10 lifts worked, so widen the claw by 5 mm
items.why: Test, change one thing, and test again.
